question.text: In the education fee example, the 6-month USDINR futures rate of 83.64 was calculated as:

explanation.text: The Logic: Current USDINR = 82. 6-month premium = 2%. Futures rate = 82 + (2% × 82) = 82 + 1.64 = 83.64. The premium added to 82 is Rs. 1.64 per USD (i.e., 164 paise), not 1.64 paise. The Trap: The 2% premium is applied to the SPOT rate, giving a Rs. 1.64 per USD increment — it is not a flat Rs. 2 addition. Note: The 2% premium reflects the interest-rate differential between India and the US for the 6-month period (interest-rate parity, p.63). Source: NISM-Series-I Currency Derivatives workbook, pp.63 and 100-101.
